A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Meta Flow Maps work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GMM and MNIST guidance experiments, ImageNet generation and posterior-sampling evaluations, and reward-steering and fine-tuning results in Section 7 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports MFM-Search evaluations and an expanded GMM MMD analysis.

M1.justification: v2 adds a distinct inference procedure, MFM-Search (Appendix A.7, Algorithm 4). It repeatedly generates posterior candidates, selects the highest-reward endpoint and re-noises it to construct the next candidate population. This substantially extends the available inference methods; the underlying MFM architecture and principal training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2D GMM inverse problem, MNIST class-mixture task and ImageNet generation, posterior-sampling, steering and fine-tuning tasks. MFM-Search is evaluated using the existing image rewards, without adding a dataset, domain or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: The ImageNet steering comparisons add MFM-Search as an evaluated alternative (v2 Figures 7 and 14). DPS and Best-of-N remain, and MFM-GF is retained in the appendix despite its omission from the main plot. Other benchmark comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a candidate-budget sweep for MFM-Search, with M ranging from 1 to 64, and evaluates reward against computational cost using NFE = 2MNK. This adds a protocol for the new method. The additional descriptions of existing Euler sampling and Best-of-N construction do not establish changed settings.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 11 extends the GMM Monte Carlo sample-count sensitivity analysis to MMD, previously reported only for selected configurations. Figures 15–17 extend cross-reward checks to MFM-Search. Existing FID ablations remain; the additional GMM density and MNIST class-ratio panels redisplay earlier analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix F.2 newly states that MNIST SMC results report mean L2 over 20 random seeds. v1 already disclosed 20 seeds for GMM SMC, but not for MNIST. This is additional repeated-run reporting, without evidence that the number of runs increased.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial MFM-Search reward-versus-compute and cross-reward results across three reward models, establishing a stronger gradient-free alternative to MFM-GF, plus GMM MMD curves. It also corrects the prose attribution of strong compute-normalised performance from MFM-GF to MFM-G. Table 2 retains MFM FIDs of 3.72, 2.40 and 1.97 at 1, 2 and 4 NFEs.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.6 derives a value-gradient identity using composed conditional MFM samples and their Jacobians. Appendix D also corrects the correlation range from 1 ≤ rho ≤ 1 to −1 ≤ rho ≤ 1. The central convergence propositions and Appendix C proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: stochastic one-step posterior sampling, efficient asymptotically exact steering, unbiased off-policy fine-tuning and strong ImageNet reward alignment. The added search method does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.7 explicitly identifies poor high-dimensional scaling of MFM-GF and characterises MFM-Search as heuristic reward maximisation without asymptotic guarantees of sampling the tilted distribution. These are substantive new applicability qualifications. The existing qualification about bias from drift rescaling remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds project and code links and documents the shared MFM-derived baseline drift, 250-step Euler steering, the 128,000-sample Best-of-N pool and grouping procedure, and MMD kernel estimation. It also supplies search and DPS NFE accounting. These improve documentation without establishing changes to previously used implementations.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds the concurrent Diamond Maps work by Holderrieth et al. (2026), distinguishing MFM's direct training from data and unbiased fine-tuning objective. Boffi reference updates and removal of the duplicate Kim entry concern retained works rather than substantive additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 standardises spelling, fixes grammar and terminology, rewrites the ImageNet steering discussion, and organises Appendix F into clearer model, reward and evaluation descriptions. The overall narrative and main section structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The ImageNet figures are substantially reorganised around NFE comparisons, with new search curves and legends and expanded appendix plots. Separate generation galleries in v1 Figures 15–23 become subsampled, matched-seed comparison grids in v2 Figures 21–22. Algorithms are reformatted, and existing GMM/MNIST panels are redisplayed alongside the new MMD plot.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects misleading attribution of MFM-G's results to MFM-GF, clarifies comparison settings and adds an evaluated gradient-free search alternative with explicit limitations. These improve accuracy, reproducibility information and practical usefulness. The search procedure lacks tilted-distribution sampling guarantees, while the central theory and principal FID results remain unchanged, making the overall gain useful but limited.
